children: President Trump has suspended implementation of most sanctions required under a recently enacted Russia sanctions law, drawing criticism from lawmakers in both parties. The decision reflects his administration’s effort to pursue negotiations with Moscow while containing energy prices ahead of the midterm elections.

For investors, the pause reduces the immediate prospect of new trade barriers targeting major buyers of Russian energy. That could ease pressure on fuel supplies and energy-dependent businesses, although any effect on prices remains uncertain. The possibility that Trump could activate the penalties later leaves oil markets and international trade exposed to further policy shifts.

The bipartisan legislation authorizes tariffs of up to 100% on leading importers of Russian oil and gas, alongside penalties against certain Russian officials and institutions. It gave the president discretion over tariff rates and allowed him to waive sanctions after notifying Congress and explaining why doing so served the national interest.

In an executive order issued Friday, Trump said he had submitted the required certification and invoked that waiver authority. The order did not publicly detail his reasoning. The move came shortly before a deadline for imposing tariffs and followed his announcement of an agreement to purchase Russian diesel.

Critics argue that easing economic pressure undermines efforts to end Russia’s war in Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the decision would embolden Moscow, while Republican Sens. Darline Graham and Ted Cruz questioned the administration’s approach. Democratic Sen. Richard Blumenthal, a co-sponsor of the legislation, said the waivers weakened a bipartisan effort to constrain Russia.

The dispute highlights a tension between limiting energy costs and using sanctions to pursue foreign-policy goals. Trump retains the option to impose the penalties later, making the current pause a reprieve rather than a permanent resolution for countries and businesses exposed to Russian energy trade.

title: Trump pauses Russia sanctions, putting energy costs ahead of economic pressure
